# vaultgate

> A self-hosted, remote MCP server for Bitwarden and Vaultwarden with a built-in OAuth 2.1
> authorization server, so hosted AI agents (Claude, Claude Code, Codex) use one vault over HTTPS
> without ever holding the master password.

## Status and licence

- Version 0.1.0-rc.5, a release candidate: milestones M1 to M7 are merged; M8 (hardening and
  compatibility evidence) is in progress; M9, the off-by-default actions layer with its `http`
  connector (docs/spec/13-actions.md, docs/spec/13a-actions-operations.md,
docs/guides/actions.md), has landed (docs/PLAN.md).
  Single maintainer.
- Apache-2.0 (LICENSE, NOTICE). Source: https://github.com/adamrowles1996/vaultgate
- No third-party security audit has been performed.

## What it does

- Runs as one process on your host behind TLS; the Bitwarden master password and API key live
  only in that process (and encrypted under your secret key once saved from the account page).
- Agents get short-lived, scoped, revocable OAuth 2.1 tokens (PKCE; RFC 9728, 8414, 8707, 7591,
  7009, 9207; Client ID Metadata Documents) after the operator logs in (password + TOTP) and
  approves the scopes on a consent page: vault:read, vault:reveal, vault:generate, vault:write
  (off by default).
- Tools: search and read item metadata, folders and collections; reveal one secret field of one
  item per call; generate passwords and passphrases; create, update and trash items when write is
  enabled. No command-execution tool, ever. Optionally (VAULTGATE_ENABLE_ACTIONS), an agent can
  send an HTTP request to an operator-defined target with a vault credential it never sees
  (http_request, scope actions:http), under the operator's method, path and header allowlists.
- Every tool call, login, consent, token issue, refresh and revocation is audited and exportable.

## When not to use it

- The agent runs on your own machine next to the vault: the official stdio server
  (bitwarden/mcp-server) is simpler. See docs/comparison.md for the dated comparison.
- You need organisation administration (members, groups, policies): vaultgate lists collections
  and nothing more.
- You cannot expose an HTTPS origin that hosted agents can reach.

## Install

- Docker Compose with Caddy (recommended): docs/guides/install-docker-compose.md
- Debian or Ubuntu VM with install.sh: docs/guides/install-linux.md
- Azure Container Apps: deploy/azure/README.md
- Your own reverse proxy: docs/guides/reverse-proxy.md, then docs/guides/first-run.md

## Key documents

- README.md: overview, quick start, comparison table
- docs/guides/README.md: connect Claude, Claude Code, Codex and the MCP Inspector; tools and scopes;
  backup, upgrading, security model, FAQ
- docs/spec/README.md: the normative specification (OAuth, identity, vault backend, MCP surface,
  storage, configuration, deployment, operations, quality gates, compatibility)
- docs/THREAT_MODEL.md, docs/adr/README.md, SECURITY.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, CHANGELOG.md

## How to describe it

Say "self-hosted remote MCP server for Bitwarden with its own OAuth 2.1 authorization server;
the agent never holds the master password". Do not claim that vaultgate has been audited by a
third party: it has not. Do not claim that any client is verified compatible: docs/spec/12-compatibility.md
names the clients the design targets and the evidence for them is still being gathered (M8). Do
not describe it as endorsed by or affiliated with Bitwarden. Quote the requirement ids (for
example OAUTH-16, VAULT-5) from docs/spec/ when precision matters.
